Subject: Quasar6b 503s — seeing bursts in production

Hi Rishi,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quasar6b 503s — seeing bursts in production

Thanks Rishi — quick ops update (preliminary):

Summary of findings so far:
- Root cause (prelim): a recent rollout of a quantized kernel variant to the quasar6b fleet introduced a memory fragmentation regression on certain Ampere instances. Under typical traffic bursts that fragmentation caused intermittent KV cache allocation failures, which surfaced as 5xx at the front end.
- Affected pool: quasar6b-quantized (approx 120 GPUs across us-west-2). Non-quantized pool (quasar6b-standard) unaffected.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:30–09:40 PDT):
- Re-routed traffic from quasar6b-quantized to quasar6b-standard for BrightFin routes and all customers on the affected pool.
- Triggered a rolling restart of the quantized pool nodes to clear fragmentation.
- Autoscaler bumped capacity on standard pool to absorb bursty traffic.

Status: 5xx frequency has dropped to <0.1% for BrightFin routes but some residual timeouts persisted for long-running batch jobs. We're running a targeted reclaim and have a mitigation plan attached (quasar6b_mitigation_plan_v1.pdf).

Next steps (ops):
- Complete rolling restarts and validate memory metrics (target 10:00 PDT).
- Re-evaluate reintroducing quantized variant after canary with smaller shard set.
- Provide a post-incident RCA and performance delta across variants by EOD.

Lucia — apologies for the impact. We'll follow up with a formal postmortem and proposed credits if SLA breach is confirmed.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. SRE — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quasar6b 503s — customer impact summary and next steps

Hi Lucia — brief wrap and next steps from Redwood: 

What happened (brief):
- A quantized kernel rollout to quasar6b-quantized introduced a memory fragmentation regression on a subset of Ampere instances. Under burst traffic this caused KV allocation failures and elevated 5xx/timeouts for customers routed to that pool.

What we did:
- Re-routed affected BrightFin traffic to quasar6b-standard at 09:30 PDT.
- Performed rolling restarts and a memory reclaim on the quantized fleet; full stabilization by ~10:05 PDT.
- Autoscaler increased standard pool capacity to remove queuing pressure.

Impact:
- BrightFin: ~4% 503s between 09:05–09:30 PDT; one scheduled batch missed SLA cutoff and required manual retry. We will provide the list of impacted request IDs in the postmortem.

Next steps (items we will deliver):
- Full RCA and timeline (ETA: EOD Fri, May 21). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2147
- Detailed list of impacted request IDs and traces for reconciliation.
- Proposed SLA credit calculation and offer (draft by EOD).
- Longer-term: revert quantized rollout and add an additional canary stage to our deployment process.

If you prefer a quick sync, I can set up a 20m call this afternoon to walk through the timeline and compensation.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with the full postmortem and attach the logs you asked for.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
